title: In silico and in vitro investigation of dual targeting Prima-1(MET) as precision therapeutic against lungs cancer.
authors: Meher, Rajesh Kumar; Mir, Showkat Ahmad; Anisetti, Siva Shanker
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小分子药物Prima-1(MET)与p53及EGFR酪氨酸激酶两个蛋白靶点的结合，虽用分子对接和MD模拟，但对象为蛋白-小分子互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: This study emphasizes the explorations of binding of Prima-1(MET) with two targets, p53 a tumor suppressor protein, and tyrosine kinase of epidermal growth factor receptor. In silico investigations reveal that Prima-1(MET) showed robust binding with both targets. Molecular docking simulations demonstrated the binding affinity of Prima-1(MET) with p53 and tyrosine kinase was found to be -38.601 kJ/mol and -38.976 kJ/mol. In addition, the stability of Prima-1(MET) was explored by molecular dynamics simulation. Prima-1(MET) attains stability in the binding site of the respective protein till the simulation period is over. Moreover, the free binding energy DeltaG(bind) was calculated by the molecular mechanics Poisson Boltzmann surface area method. The DeltaG(bind) of Prima-1(MET) with tyrosine kinase was found to be -58.585 +/- 0.327 kJ/mol and with p53 it was -35.910 +/- 0.335 kJ/mol. Next, cytotoxicity of the Prima-1(MET) was evaluated using multiple cancer cell lines and the IC(50) value were ranging between 4.5 and 30 muM. The cell death was identified by apoptosis assay. Further, the p53 and tyrosine kinase expression was monitored using immunofluorescence techniques, it was found Prima-1(MET) induces the expression of p53 protein and mimics the level of tyrosine kinase oncogenic target. Also, reactive oxygen species (ROS) and membrane potential activity of Prima-1(MET) was evaluated by using a lung cancer cell line. A significant decrease in intracellular ROS was observed and resulted in disruption of mitochondrial transmembrane potential. This study uncovers the underlying mechanism of Prima-1(MET) and could be helpful to design further leads against lung cancers.Communicated by Ramaswamy H. Sarma.
abstract_zh: 本研究重点探讨了Prima-1(MET)与两个靶点——肿瘤抑制蛋白p53及表皮生长因子受体的酪氨酸激酶——的结合情况。计算机模拟研究揭示，Prima-1(MET)与这两个靶点均表现出强效结合。分子对接模拟显示，Prima-1(MET)与p53和酪氨酸激酶的结合亲和力分别为-38.601 kJ/mol和-38.976 kJ/mol。此外，通过分子动力学模拟探索了Prima-1(MET)的稳定性。在模拟期间，Prima-1(MET)在相应蛋白的结合位点内保持稳定直至模拟结束。同时，利用分子力学泊松-玻尔兹曼表面积方法计算了自由结合能DeltaG(bind)。Prima-1(MET)与酪氨酸激酶的DeltaG(bind)为-58.585 +/- 0.327 kJ/mol，与p53的为-35.910 +/- 0.335 kJ/mol。接下来，使用多种癌细胞系评估了Prima-1(MET)的细胞毒性，IC(50)值范围在4.5至30 μM之间。通过凋亡实验确定了细胞死亡。进一步，利用免疫荧光技术监测了p53和酪氨酸激酶的表达，发现Prima-1(MET)诱导p53蛋白表达，并模拟酪氨酸激酶致癌靶点的水平。此外，使用肺癌细胞系评估了Prima-1(MET)的活性氧（ROS）和膜电位活性。观察到细胞内ROS显著减少，并导致线粒体跨膜电位破坏。本研究揭示了Prima-1(MET)的潜在机制，可能有助于设计针对肺癌的进一步先导化合物。由Ramaswamy H. Sarma通讯。
